label: copy-phase input w (rare, very low precision)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.1% of sequences). 99% of its activation mass is in the copy phase, and about 72% of the mass is on steps where the fed-back input is w. Most of the rest is on copy-phase inputs m or d, plus some 0. It is biased toward later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3, longer sequences L=8-9) and toward steps whose output token (the token after w) is 0, i, d or s. It almost never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter. Precision is very low: only about 0.5% of copy-phase w steps activate, and adding the output-token or position conditions only raises precision to about 5%. Whatever selects the rare active instances is not captured by the available token or position variables. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12 of max 0.22), and no variable clearly modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=d (+4.71), phase=2 & in_tok=m (+4.50), out_tok=d (+3.76), out_tok=i (+3.71), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+3.59), out_tok=0 (+3.58). Lower it: correct=1 (-4.67), to_go=7 (-2.59), prev_tok=n (-2.19), to_go=5 (-2.04).
